title: Where each retriever embarrasses itself
intro: Two queries, one corpus. Semantic search returns a filing ID one digit off. Keyword search returns nothing at all. Neither is broken — they fail in opposite directions, and the query class tells you which one you are about to hit.

provenance.source: a narrated retrieval bake-off over a 620-filing UCC corpus and a 200-query set; scores, ranks and fusion arithmetic are plausible inventions, not measurements

foot: The mechanism this walks is M09's Hybrid Retrieval over UCC Filings — keyword and semantic fused by reciprocal rank fusion, then a cross-encoder rerank over the fused top-N.

steps.title: Two queries, opposite failures
narrative: Query A is a lookup: pull filing 2024-FL-0012345. Query B is a concept: which debtors pledged not-yet-acquired equipment? The corpus is the same 620 filings for both.

Semantic search nails B and fails A. To an embedding model 2024-FL-0012345 and 2024-FL-0012354 are near-identical strings, and the wrong one scores 0.981 against the right one's 0.979. It returns a different debtor's filing at rank 1, with high confidence and no signal that anything went wrong.

Keyword search is the mirror image. It puts 2024-FL-0012345 at rank 1 on an exact token match, and on query B it returns nothing usable — not one filing in the corpus contains the phrase "not-yet-acquired". They all say hereafter acquired.
steps.youDo: Split your own query log into exact-identifier and conceptual queries and count each pile. The ratio decides which retriever's failure mode you will be living with.

1. 2024-FL-0012354  cos 0.981   NORTHBAY MARINE SUPPLY INC   <- wrong debtor
2. 2024-FL-0012543  cos 0.980
3. 2024-FL-0012435  cos 0.979

cells: no — the right one is rank 4 at 0.979

steps.title: Hybrid fuses the rankings, not the scores
narrative: Because the two retrievers fail in opposite directions, the useful move is not choosing between them. Run both and fuse. Reciprocal rank fusion scores each document by 1 / (k + rank) summed across rankings, with k = 60 — it uses only positions, so a cosine of 0.981 and a BM25 score of 14.2 never have to be made comparable.

Watch the arithmetic on query A. The wrong filing is rank 0 in semantic and rank 8 in keyword: 1/60 + 1/68 = 0.031373. The right filing is rank 3 in semantic and rank 0 in keyword: 1/63 + 1/60 = 0.032540. The correct answer wins by about a thousandth.

That margin is the honest picture of hybrid. It is not a resounding victory, it is one retriever's confident mistake being outvoted by the other retriever's confident correctness — which is exactly what you wanted, and exactly why the win is narrow rather than dramatic.
steps.claudeSays: Neither retriever changed its mind. Fusion changed which one gets to be right about this query class.

terminal.text: rank 1: 2024-FL-0012345  ACME LOGISTICS & DISTRIBUTION, L.L.C.   <- correct
rank 1: 2024-FL-0019988  "...now owned or hereafter acquired"     <- correct

view.text: A cosine of 0.981 and a BM25 of 14.2 live on incompatible scales, and normalising them means inventing a weighting you cannot defend. RRF throws the scores away and keeps only the ordering, which is the part both retrievers actually agree on the meaning of.

steps.title: The rerank that rescues rank 7
narrative: Query C mixes both classes: which active liens cover inventory as well as equipment? — a concept plus a constraint. Hybrid puts the gold chunk at fused rank 7. The window takes the top 5. The right answer was retrieved and then discarded twenty milliseconds before the model saw anything.

You could raise top_k to 10 and pay for five more chunks on every query forever. The cheaper fix is a second pass: send the fused top-50 to a cross-encoder, which scores each candidate jointly with the query rather than comparing two independently-computed vectors, and reorder. The gold chunk moves from 7 to 1.

The cost of that pass is 50 cross-encoder scores — about 40ms and $0.0002 — against the 35,500 evidence tokens it would take to brute-force the same result by retrieving the whole top-50 into the window. This is the cheapest accuracy in the retrieval stack, and it is the fix for M08's RANK failure specifically.
steps.youDo: Log the fused rank of the chunk that actually answered each query. If it is regularly outside your top_k, you need a rerank, not a bigger top_k.

terminal.text: which active liens cover inventory as well as equipment?
gold 2024-FL-0012345#collateral at fused rank 7  —  top_k=5, it never enters the window
top = rerank(q, cands, k=5)   # cross-encoder, 50 pairs

cells: scored jointly with the query: both terms, status active
vs. 35,500 evidence tokens to brute-force it

steps.title: The scoreboard, including where the pipeline is overhead
narrative: Two hundred queries, split 50 exact-identifier / 40 exact-name / 60 paraphrased concept / 50 concept-plus-constraint, run through all four strategies. Keyword lands at 60%, semantic at 74%, hybrid at 90%, hybrid-plus-rerank at 95%.

Read it by row rather than by total. Keyword is perfect on exact IDs and semantic gets 62% of them — if your workload is a filing-lookup service, the fanciest pipeline on this page is 41ms of latency and a model call per query for zero additional points, and plain BM25 is the correct engineering answer. Semantic beats keyword by 58 points on paraphrase and would be the right single choice for a prose-only corpus with no identifiers in it.

The rerank earns its keep in exactly one place: concept-plus-constraint, where it adds 17 points because that is the class where the right chunk is regularly present but buried. Everywhere else it is a rounding error. Match the strategy to the query class, and be willing to conclude that the sophisticated option is not worth wiring up.
steps.youDo: Build this table for your own corpus with your own query classes. The row where your current strategy scores worst is the only place worth spending effort.

views.text: No retriever is best; each is best at a query class, and the mix in your log decides. Fuse when the log is mixed, rerank when the gold chunk keeps landing just below top_k, and ship plain keyword without embarrassment when the workload is identifiers.
